rules.description: The market's rate of travel over the last `nearBars` bars is at least K times its rate over the `farBars` bars before them — the trend is steepening. Direction-agnostic: both rates are absolute, so both sides are identical text.
rules.pseudocode: AbsValue(close[0] - close[nearBars]) * farBars >= accelMultiple * AbsValue(close[nearBars] - close[nearBars + farBars]) * nearBars

complexity.reason: three lagged closes and a cross-multiplied comparison; no persistent state

catalog_match.note: that rule is an EXIT, requires both legs SIGNED in the trade's direction, and pins the windows equal (legBars and 2 x legBars); this is an Entry context filter on ABSOLUTE rates with independent windows, so it fires on a different set of bars and an Exit cannot sit in the entry pane anyway

rules.merge_notes: One source. Grimes gives 'trend rate' no formula; it reduces to a ratio of two displacement rates. Cross-multiplied so no division rounds, the MinRewardToRiskFilter spelling. Sides `same` because absolute values carry no direction — place it beside a directional rule. Cited as a buying-climax sign, so climax_termination may want it too.

rules.description: The moving average is higher now than `slopeLookback` bars ago (long) / lower (short) — Grimes's trend filter, and, at a length multiplied by `htfMultiplier`, his higher-timeframe alignment filter.

complexity.reason: an EMA compared with its own lagged value

catalog_match.note: EmaSlope at `slopeAtr = 0` IS this test, exactly; no input to add

rules.merge_notes: RECONCILED: indicators_bands' identical row is folded in here, bringing G03-29 (the same rising-average test at maLength 50, with Grimes's flat dead zone, which is EmaSlope's slopeAtr above 0). Four restatements collapse: G07-02 is the trading-timeframe slope, G07-25 and G03-35 the same test at `emaLength x htfMultiplier` (both 5). `EmaSlope(slopeAtr = 0)` reproduces all three, so the higher-timeframe filter is a GRID choice, not a rule. G03-35 writes a simple `Average`; EmaSlope is exponential, the settled series.

rules.description: At least a fraction of the last `lookback` closes sit above the moving average (long) / below it (short) — 'price spends a lot of time on one side of the average' as a with-trend context gate.
rules.pseudocode: CountIF(close > ema(close, emaLength), lookback) >= fracThreshold * lookback

complexity.reason: a CountIF over a window against an EMA read at each counted bar's own offset

catalog_match.note: the same K-of-N test on the same EMA; Grimes's fraction is `minBarsBeyond = round(fracThreshold x lookback)`, i.e. 14 of 20

rules.merge_notes: One source, no new content: `BarsBeyondEmaCount(lookback 20, minBarsBeyond 14, emaLength 20)` is Grimes's filter. Kept apart from the run form `ConsecutiveClosesBeyondEmaRun`, which the catalog already separates. Grimes does not commit to SMA vs EMA for this generic reference average; the catalog rule is exponential, and he says explicitly that he does not trade it mechanically.

rules.description: Equity lost since the first bar of the current calendar day exceeds the limit — blocks entries and forces flat for the rest of the day.
rules.pseudocode:
if (Date[0] <> Date[1]) dayStartEquity = NetProfit + OpenPositionProfit;
(NetProfit + OpenPositionProfit) - dayStartEquity <= -dailyLossLimit

complexity.reason: a persistent period-start latch plus a date-boundary reset; both are precedented — MonthlyProfitTarget captures period-start equity and mirrors the EL variable's history in endOfFileHook, MaxTradesPerSession resets on Date <> Date[1] — so no new engine accessor is needed

catalog_match.note: same construction with the boundary moved from Month(Date) <> Month(Date[1]) to Date <> Date[1] and the comparison on the LOSS side; EquityDrawdownFilter is the rolling-window cousin and resets at no boundary, a different accessor pattern

rules.merge_notes: Grimes gives no figure, so 1000 is a placeholder for the grid. His week and month forms are the same rule at a different boundary test, worth a `periodSelect` input only if the grid wants them. Unlike MaxTradesPerSession, which makes its exit half inert deliberately, forcing flat is WANTED here — MonthlyProfitTarget's Switch behaviour.

rules.description: The number of trades taken in the current session has reached the cap — blocks further entries until the period rolls over.

catalog_match.note: same cap, same counting rule, same default

design_decisions.recommended: ONE mechanizable trend test: `EmaSlope` (emaLength 20, slopeLookback 5, with `slopeAtr` as the optimizer input; slopeAtr = 0 is the bare slope all three Grimes restatements give). HIGHER-TIMEFRAME APPROXIMATION: the same rule at `emaLength x 5` — a second placement, not a new rule — which is the mining brief's longer-lookback-on-the-same-bars convention with the multiplier pinned at 5. Later buckets that need a structural higher-timeframe read rather than a slope should use the same 5x multiplier on a window rule (TouchOfRecentExtreme, RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple, CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh) instead of raising a fresh decision. Any bucket meeting 'the higher time frame is trending' should cite EmaSlope at 5x length and grade the rule on its own merits rather than C. The pivot-based alternative, SwingTrendHigherHighsAndLows, is authored as a B rule but is NOT the default: it needs the pivot scan and lags by `strength` bars.

design_decisions.topic: Period-scoped account switches (daily loss limit, trades per period)
options: no accessor exists; grade research and defer
design a new per-period counter and equity latch in the engine
reuse the measured MonthlyProfitTarget and MaxTradesPerSession constructions
design_decisions.recommended: Reuse. The machinery exists and is measured, so neither candidate is research. `MaxTradesPerSession` already counts entries per session with a date-boundary reset (`mp <> 0 and mp <> mp[1]`, catching reversals) and caps them — Grimes's per-period trade limit is that rule verbatim, priority D. `MonthlyProfitTarget` already captures period-start equity from NetProfit + OpenPositionProfit, blocks entries and forces flat — a daily loss limit is that construction with the boundary moved to `Date <> Date[1]` and the comparison on the loss side, priority B, no new engine accessor. Week and month variants are the same rules at a different boundary test; add a `periodSelect` input only if the grid asks for it.

bucket_summary: Eleven candidates, five rules out, four dropped as compositions (the fourth being the G07-27 stray from exits_targets) and one sent to swing_structure; the reconciliation pass also folded indicators_bands' MovingAverageSlopeTrendFilter row into this bucket's row of that key. The bucket is dominated by one test restated three times — a moving-average slope, at the trading length and at a 5x 'higher timeframe' length — which is the catalog's EmaSlope at slopeAtr = 0, so it is D, and the higher-timeframe read becomes a grid choice rather than a rule. Grimes's price-mostly-above-the-average filter is likewise BarsBeyondEmaCount, and his per-period trade cap is MaxTradesPerSession verbatim. The A list is one rule, TrendRateAcceleration; the B list is one, DailyLossLimit.
